title: Bulletproof Investing Performance Update: Week 62
text:
Safety First: Sprint Racer McKenna Haase and her helmet (via Racing News )
Bulletproof Investing: Week 62 Performance Each week, since the beginning of June 2017, I have presented at least two hedged portfolios created by Portfolio Armor to my Bulletproof Investing subscribers. This is an " investing with a helmet on " approach, and these portfolios are designed to last six months at most. As with any investment method, the returns with this approach will vary. But in the interests of transparency and accountability, I have promised to publicly share the final performance of everything I present, regardless of how it does.
Here, I update the final performance of the five hedged portfolios and the top 10 names (unhedged) that I presented in the 62nd week I offered my service. Let's look at what I presented in week 62 and how it did.
Portfolio 1 This was the $30,000 portfolio. The primary securities here were Luminex ( LMNX ) and Insperity ( NSP ). They were selected because they had the highest potential return estimates, net of hedging costs, when hedging against a >13% decline, and they had share prices low enough that you could buy a round lot of one of them for less than $10,000. Fiesta Restaurant ( FRGI ) was added in a fine-tuning step to absorb leftover cash from rounding down to round lots of the first two names.
The image above was generated by Portfolio Armor on August 2 and presented in this Marketplace post at the time.
The worst-case scenario for this portfolio was a decline of 11.47% (the "max drawdown"), and the best-case scenario was a gain of 36.33% (the "Net Potential Return" or aggregate potential return net of hedging cost). The "Expected Return" of 11.71% was a ballpark estimate taking into account that actual returns, historically, have averaged 0.3x Portfolio Armor's potential return estimates.
Portfolio 1 Performance Here's how the portfolio did, net of hedging and trading costs.
This portfolio was down 7.39%, underperforming its expected return and underperforming the SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF ( SPY ). The flat line of the portfolio toward the end of the chart is due to 2 of the positions being exited in mid-January, just before their hedges expired.

Top Names Time-Stamped For a few months, in addition to posting those top names in my Seeking Alpha Marketplace service, I also time-stamped them on Twitter. If you click on the tweet shown below and scroll down, it will take you to a thread showing those time-stamped posts as well as charts of their subsequent performance.
Week 62 Assessment The top 10 names (unhedged) underperformed SPY for the 19th time out of 60 weeks (we didn't post the top 10 in week 1). None of the hedged portfolios this week outperformed their expected returns, as all had negative returns, but the top names one hedged against a >9% drawdown outperformed SPY. Our challenging streak continued in week 62.
We still suggest investors consider splitting their assets into two or three tranches, if possible, and investing in one hedged portfolio now, one in a month or two, and so on. That way, you'll have four to six entries per year (since each hedged portfolio lasts six months), reducing the amount of money that would be exposed to a significant market transition.
